# ippon

> Run decision models on Apple silicon with typed answers and their creators' published weights.

## Start

- `ippon setup`: choose a model for this Mac, download it and connect agents (`--use claude,codex,opencode,pi,hermes`).
- `ippon claude`, `ippon codex`, `ippon opencode`, `ippon pi`, `ippon hermes`: that agent for one session, with the model beside it.
- `ippon start`, `ippon status --json`, `ippon stop`: the background server; `ippon remove AGENT|login|all` undoes setup.
- `ippon skills`: guides for agents. Read `ippon skills ippon` first. `ippon skills --path` prints their folder,
  to copy or link into the agent's skills folder.
- `ippon recommend --json`: available builds and their fit on this Mac.
- `ippon check MODEL --json`: support and memory estimate; a complete recorded download works offline.
- `ippon pull MODEL`: explicitly download the model. A name loads the commit its answers were checked at.
- Starter requests are in docs/evaluating.md, and `ippon lint request.json --json` checks one.

## Shared inference

- `ippon mcp [MODEL ...]`: stdio MCP tools: decide, models, recommend, lint.
- MCP clients share one local HTTP server and do not load model weights themselves.
- `ippon serve MODEL [NAME=MODEL ...] --detach --json`: background server, actual URL, PID and log.
- `ippon decide MODEL request.json --server --json`: use the shared server.
- `ippon status --json` (or `ippon ps`): server/model/memory status.
- `ippon stop [MODEL] [--port PORT] [--all] --json`: stop the only server, or the selected one. With several
  servers and no selection it stops none and lists them.
- HTTP: POST /v1/decide (the Sqwish SDK's format); POST /v1/systemone?diagnostics=1; POST /v1/decisions (Perplexity's
  and SGLang's formats); GET /v1/models; GET /v1/status; GET /health.
- Pass IPPON_API_KEY when the server requires authentication.

## Request and result

- Request: state plus questions keyed by caller-selected IDs.
- noul: instructions; answer is P(yes).
- choice: instructions and criteria labels/descriptions; answer includes every option's probability.
- score: instructions and an ordered scale of levels, within the model's limit. The answer is the creator's score
  with every level's probability, and `Answer.expected_level` in Python gives the expected level.
- Answers are under `answers`; inspect `usage`, optional `truncated`, and `diagnostics` provenance.
- Ask questions about one state together; use lint to catch ambiguous or overlapping choices.
- Models may refuse unsupported media; image URLs are never fetched.
- Weight-changing precision options and experimental kernels require explicit selection; memory pressure never
  substitutes a different model. Bare families can resolve to a published quantized build; use FAMILY:TAG to pin it.

## Failure handling

- JSON CLI errors: error.type, error.message, error.exit_code; nonzero process exit.
- MCP tool errors: isError=true, structuredContent.error; JSON-RPC errors for malformed protocol messages.
- HTTP503 overloaded includes Retry-After: wait, rather than start another copy of the model.
- Exit codes: 1 decision_error (with --server also unauthorized, forbidden, not_found, internal), 3 invalid_request, 4 unsupported_model, 5 context_too_long, 6 insufficient_memory,
  7 unsupported_profile, 8 overloaded (with --server also timeout), 9 unavailable, 10 model_not_found, 11 license_not_accepted (accept the
  model's licence with `ippon pull MODEL --accept-license`), 12 insufficient_disk (free disk space, then pull again),
  13 download_failed (repeat the pull to resume it), 14 runtime_unavailable (install or repair what the message
  names).
- Model downloads are explicit. MCP automatic startup uses downloaded models and offline Hub access.
- Direct Decider.load in Python owns a separate model; HTTP shares the server's pool.
